sources: GeoTIFF driver supports integer and floating raster band types including Float32 and Float64.
GeoTIFF nodata may be stored in TIFFTAG_GDAL_NODATA for the default GDALGeoTIFF profile.
The GeoTIFF nodata tag is dataset-wide in practice and all bands must share the same nodata value.
GeoTIFF can carry an internal transparency mask recognized from FILETYPE_MASK.
Internal masks are exposed as full 8-bit masks by default, typically 0 invalid and 255 valid.
External or internal overview masks are distinct from the full-resolution main-band mask.
SPARSE_OK can omit blocks whose pixels are all nodata or zero; storage sparsity must not be confused with elevation value semantics.
A zero-valued block is not automatically nodata when no nodata metadata or mask establishes invalidity.
GeoTIFF georeferencing may come from multiple sources whose priority can be configured; provenance must pin the source used.
GeoTIFF compression and predictor settings are storage details and must not alter decoded lossless pixel values.
DISCARD_LSB is explicitly lossy and is excluded from terminal elevation inputs.
Lossy JPEG/JXL-style compression is unsuitable for terminal exact elevation pixel identity.
Tile/strip organization and block size affect access layout rather than the raster grid definition.
Streaming reads impose file-layout constraints but do not change the requirement for exact decoded pixel identity.
A full-resolution raster band has the dataset width and height.
Each raster band has an explicit GDAL data type.
A raster band can have a single nodata value.
A raster band can also have a nodata or transparency mask band.
Scale and offset metadata can transform stored raster samples into meaningful physical values.
A raster band can carry a unit name that is relevant for elevation interpretation.
AREA_OR_POINT distinguishes area-sample versus point-sample semantics but does not change georeferencing interpretation.
Stored minimum and maximum metadata are optional and are not proof of a fresh exhaustive scan.
STATISTICS_VALID_PERCENT records the fraction of valid non-nodata pixels used in statistics.
Overviews cover the same geographic region with fewer pixels than the full-resolution raster.
Overview selection is software logic and cannot silently replace base-resolution terminal pixels.
Arbitrary overviews may be synthesized by gateways that downsample remotely.
Some algorithms can internally reduce precision, so exact-value paths must preserve source dtype/value semantics.
-srcwin selects an exact pixel/line source window.
A source window extending outside a raster can be filled with zero when nodata is absent.
-epo can make partially outside source windows fail instead of accepting fill.
-eco only errors for completely outside windows and is weaker than -epo for exact-domain guards.
-ovr NONE forces the base-resolution source instead of an overview.
AUTO overview selection may choose reduced-resolution data and is non-terminal for exact pixels.
-outsize changes raster dimensions and therefore invokes resampling.
-tr requests target resolution and can invoke resampling.
The default nearest resampler is still a resampling path when output dimensions or resolution differ.
Bilinear, cubic, spline, Lanczos, average, RMS and mode all alter or aggregate source sample selection.
-scale changes pixel values and is excluded from raw-value terminal parity.
Applying -unscale commonly requires an explicit output dtype to avoid information loss.
-a_scale and -a_offset assign metadata without themselves modifying pixel values.
-strict can fail conversions that would otherwise lose unsupported information.
-projwin is georeferenced-window selection and can expand to pixel boundaries under nearest-neighbor behavior.
-projwin_srs changes coordinate interpretation but does not reproject the raster.
Rasterio GDAL-style valid-data masks use non-zero values, typically 255, for valid pixels.
Rasterio masked arrays use the inverse sense: True means invalid.
Rasterio documents an exact inverse relation between read(masked=True).mask and read_masks().
A valid numeric zero can coexist with nodata value zero in low-dynamic-range data, so mask provenance matters.
A .msk sidecar can override nodata metadata for mask interpretation.
Dataset mask precedence first considers .msk, dataset alpha, or internal mask.
For RGBA with shadow nodata, alpha can determine the dataset mask.
When only nodata exists, dataset_mask uses band-mask logic rather than treating all zeros as invalid by fiat.
If no nodata or mask exists, dataset_mask reports all pixels valid.
Per-band read_masks and dataset_mask have different semantics and must not be silently substituted.
Rasterio exposes dataset dtypes per band.
Rasterio exposes dataset nodata and per-band nodatavals.
Rasterio exposes mask_flag_enums to distinguish nodata, alpha, per-dataset, and all-valid masks.
Rasterio read(window=...) supports exact windowed reads without boundless behavior by default.
boundless=True permits reads beyond dataset extent and can return filled pixels; terminal reads keep it false.
read(out_shape=...) can change output dimensions and therefore is non-terminal for raw pixel identity.
The read resampling parameter can select algorithms beyond raw/base-resolution reading.
window_transform returns the affine transform for a dataset window and enables parent-window parity checks.
Dataset files metadata can expose sidecar files that participate in nodata or georeferencing interpretation.
The driver property allows a strict GeoTIFF-driver identity check on downloaded coverage bytes.
EA WCS is intended to return raw pixel data including elevation values rather than rendered colors.
EA publishes a distinct LIDAR Composite DTM 1m WCS service separate from DSM.
EA WCS uses OGC WCS 2.0.1 for composite elevation services.
WCS GetCoverage response bytes require SHA256 plus grid/value digest before use.
Terminal WCS retrieval prohibits scaling, interpolation, overview, warp, and resize.
Terminal WCS axis order must be explicit rather than guessed.
Cold-cache and refreshed-cache WCS replays must preserve metadata and raster-value digests.
Native-tile versus WCS parity is required when both acquisition paths are available.
Outside-domain zero fill is rejected as elevation.
Raw stored sample parity and physical-value parity are separate checks when scale/offset metadata exists.
Nodata metadata parity and validity-mask parity are separate checks.
Base-resolution pixel-set parity must precede extrema/tie-set parity.
Exact extrema require exhaustive valid-pixel scanning rather than cached approximate statistics.
All tied min/max members must reconcile by global pixel identity, not only by numeric extrema values.
